items.title: Moises and SoundCloud Partner to Bring AI-Supported Creation, Collaboration and Distribution Together for 150+ Million Artists
items.excerpt: Moises, the ethically trained AI creative suite used by 80 million musicians, is partnering with SoundCloud to bring stem separation, chord/lyric detection and AI-assisted mixing and mastering together with SoundCloud distribution. SoundCloud says it does not train generative models on artists' music without consent.

items.title: As fans reject AI-generated music, even boosters are drawing the line
items.excerpt: Guardian analysis: streaming services, musicians and fans are drawing lines on AI-generated music, and even enthusiasts like Grimes and A$AP Rocky say they embrace AI content but won't produce it themselves. (Background mentions Spotify's 50m-track slop removal, which was already covered; this piece takes the wider artist-sentiment angle.)

items.title: AI 음악 기술 '뉴튠', 오디오비주얼 에이전트 DJ '탈' ADE 2026서 첫 공개
items.excerpt: Korean AI music company Neutune is premiering 'Tal', an audiovisual agent DJ built on traditional Korean mask motifs, at Amsterdam Dance Event 2026. The project was made with KOCCA's 2026 AI content production grant.

items.title: Korea's JYP Partners and SM pursue AI idols to personalize fan service
items.excerpt: K-pop agencies JYP (via JYP Partners) and SM are pursuing AI idols and backing startups to test personalized AI idol fan services and build new IP.

items.title: Elephant In the Room Reminder: Major Hits from Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave Already Used to Train AI Without Compensation, the ICMP Tells Australian Legislators
items.excerpt: Global publishers' body ICMP told Australian legislators that AI models have already been trained on songs by Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave without permission or payment, and warned that a text-and-data-mining carve-out would 'legitimize larceny'.

items.title: Is There a Future for 'Humanoid Robot Performances'? South Korea's Galaxy Corporation Thinks So
items.excerpt: Galaxy Corporation, a Korean 'physical AI' entertainment-tech company combining K-pop IP, AI and humanoid robots, is staging a Halloween robot-performance event in Saratoga, California on October 30. Weak AI angle: the AI is about robotics more than the music itself.

items.title: Chronixx calls for separate Grammy category for AI albums
items.excerpt: Ahead of the 2027 Grammy race, reggae singer Chronixx has called for albums made with large language models and machine learning to compete in their own Grammy category. In reggae and dancehall, the AI debate already covers songwriting, visuals, voice imitation and training data.

items.title: Lithuanian lawmakers propose legal protection against AI voice cloning
items.excerpt: Lithuanian MPs proposed Civil Code amendments creating a legal right to one's voice, so reproducing, publishing or otherwise using it, including AI-generated imitations, would need consent. Music angle is indirect: this is a general voice-likeness law.
